title.text: What is the title of the study?
title.purpose: Identifying the study in every listing and letter about it
title.extractionPrompt: Find the study's full title, as given on the cover page or at the head of the synopsis. Give it exactly as written, without the word 'Title', a protocol number or a version.

sponsor.text: Who is the sponsor of the study?
sponsor.purpose: Who answers for the study to regulators and to the institution
sponsor.extractionPrompt: Find the organisation named as the sponsor, usually on the cover page, a sponsor information page or the synopsis. Give its name as written. When an investigator is the sponsor, give their name.

leadInvestigator.purpose: Who is accountable for the study, and who the review corresponds with
leadInvestigator.extractionPrompt: Find the principal investigator, study chair or lead investigator, usually on the cover page, the study team page or the signature page. Give the person's name only, without degrees or titles. When several are named, give the one the document calls principal or lead.

phase.purpose: How much is already known about the product, and how much oversight the trial needs
phase.extractionPrompt: Find the trial phase as the protocol states it, usually in the title, on the cover page or in the synopsis. When the protocol states no phase, choose no phase.

allocation.text: How are participants assigned to the study's arms?
allocation.purpose: Whether a difference between arms can be put down to the intervention
allocation.extractionPrompt: Decide how the protocol assigns participants to arms, from its design section or synopsis.

singleArm.label: Not assigned
singleArm.description: A single arm, so everyone receives the same intervention

masking.text: Who is kept from knowing which intervention a participant receives?
masking.purpose: How far the results can be biased by knowing who received what
masking.extractionPrompt: Find whether the trial is open-label or blinded, and how many parties are blinded: participants, investigators, outcome assessors, care providers.

double.label: Two or more parties: double-blind or more

sampleSize.text: How many participants will be enrolled?
sampleSize.purpose: Whether the study's size matches its aims, and the burden it puts on participants
sampleSize.extractionPrompt: Find the planned total number of participants to be enrolled, across all arms and sites, usually in the synopsis or the sample size section. When the protocol gives a number to randomise and a larger number to screen, give the number to enrol or randomise.

minimumAge.text: What is the youngest age a participant can be, in years?
minimumAge.purpose: Whether children take part, which changes how consent is obtained
minimumAge.extractionPrompt: Find the minimum age in the inclusion criteria, in years.

sex.text: Who can take part, by sex?
sex.purpose: Whether the study is open to everyone it could apply to
sex.extractionPrompt: Decide from the eligibility criteria whether the study enrols women only, men only, or both.

healthyVolunteers.text: Does the study enrol healthy volunteers?
healthyVolunteers.purpose: Whether people with nothing to gain from the intervention are exposed to it
healthyVolunteers.extractionPrompt: Decide from the eligibility criteria whether people without the condition under study can take part.

kinds.text: What kinds of intervention does the study test?
kinds.purpose: Which regulations apply to the products and procedures used
kinds.extractionPrompt: Find every intervention the study assigns to participants, including any comparator such as a placebo or usual care, and pick the kind each one is.

behavioral.label: Behavioural
behavioral.description: Such as counselling, education or exercise

primaryOutcome.text: What is the primary outcome measure?
primaryOutcome.purpose: Whether the study measures what its objective asks
primaryOutcome.extractionPrompt: Find the primary outcome or endpoint. When several are listed, give the first. Name what is measured, without when it is measured.
